title: Reset Week - Commander Brief & Messaging Play (v0.1)
content:
PURPOSE
---
Working commander-style brief for the company reset week (internal planning doc). Goal: align exec asks, run-of-show, prework, and decision triggers so the town reset is tight, fast, and de-conflicted. This is intentionally terse — use as an operational checklist + messaging source for the all-hands and exec readout.

OVERVIEW (one-liner)
---
Two-day reset week in the first week of Q2: sync exec priorities, publish condensed micro-OKRs, roll decisions into team-level sprint commitments. Outcome = single prioritized list of scoped deliverables + escalation matrix.

SCHEDULE (high level)
---
Day 0 (prep, asynchronous, 3 days before): teams submit 2-slide micro-OKR + risk statement into RH tracker (ENG-3142).
Day 1 (leadership/day): executive readouts 09:00–12:00, cross-functional breakout 13:30–17:00, decision triage 17:30–18:30.
Day 2 (all-hands + team sync): company all-hands 10:00–11:00, leader micro‑sessions 11:30–15:30, final roll & publish 16:00–17:00.

RUN-OF-SHOW (quick)
---
- Exec readouts (09:00–12:00): 8 x 15min + 5min buffer, each exec: status, top 3 asks, 1 risk with mitigation.
- Breakouts (13:30): engineering, product, go-to-market, ops/legal — each generates 3 action items and a blocker list.
- Decision triage (17:30): Ops committee irrevocably decides items tagged "make-or-break".
- All-hands (Day 2): CEO context (10m) -> 3 priority commitments (10m) -> Hot seat decisions (10m) -> Q&A (15m).

MICRO-OKR FORMAT (submitted by teams)
---
1) One-line objective (2–6 words)
2) Top 3 measurable key results (metric + target)
3) Scope / in-scope & out-of-scope bullets (1–3 lines)
4) Risk (1 line) + guardrail (if triggered, who owns escalation)
5) Dependencies (Jira keys)

PRIORITIZATION RATIONALE (quick)
---
- Business signal: revenue impact, retention, platform reliability score.
- Customer-safety: compliance/regulatory tasks have immediate precedence.
- Cost/operational: tasks with >20% unit-cost improvement or critical latency wins.
- Learning/strategic bets: limited to 10% of sprint capacity.

DECISION TRIGGERS (examples)
---
- If a task increases latency SLO risk > 5% -> route to SRE lead (Luca).
- If projected burn > committed capacity for Dedicated customers -> finance + product review.
- If ETA slips > 2 weeks for a cross-team ship -> canary rollback or scope reduce.

COMMUNICATIONS & MESSAGING (staging)
---
Audience: employees, customers (targets), partners.
- Employee all-hands script (short):
  - CEO: high-level context (focus, tradeoffs), commit to 3 things we will deliver in 90 days.
  - Product lead: what changes for developers (APIs, SLAs).
  - Eng lead: where we will tighten reliability and cost.
- External customer brief (post-reset): one-pager: what customers can expect operationally + any impact windows. Draft owner: Priya.
- FAQ (internal): canonical answers for likely questions (billing, Dedicated capacity, private deployment timelines).

RACI (core)
---
- Commander (overall): Maya Chen (owner of doc/final publish)
- Exec readouts coordinator: Ethan Rivera
- Run logistics: People Ops + Events (vendor: Arium)
- Decision triage chair: CTO (Priya Nair backup: Head of SRE)

RISKS & MITIGATIONS (working list)
---
1) Risk: exec readouts run long -> Mitigation: strict timekeeper + pre-read required.
2) Risk: teams miss prework -> Mitigation: block 2 hours of prep time on calendar + incentive.
3) Risk: conflicting high-priority asks across teams -> Mitigation: triage matrix (business impact X feasibility), CEO tie-break.
4) Risk: external leak of internal roadmap -> Mitigation: redact user-impact specifics in customer-facing doc, legal review.

UNRESOLVED QUESTIONS (actionable)
---
- Should we require Design to provide a "dev-impact" estimate as part of micro-OKR? (ask @Design leads)
- What is the guardrail for re-prioritizing Dedicated capacity mid-quarter? (finance + product)
- Do we publish the entire risk register externally or only top-line items? (Legal + Revenue)

ACTION ITEM BACKLOG (initial)
---
- [ ] Template micro-OKR slide (Maya) — due 2026-03-11 (in progress)
- [ ] Pre-reads collated and shared (Ethan) — due 2026-03-12
- [ ] All-hands script draft (Priya) — due 2026-03-12
- [ ] Customer-facing one-pager (Priya) — due 2026-03-15
- [ ] Decision triage rubric (CTO office) — due 2026-03-13

NOTES TO SELF / SQUINT TESTS
---
- Keep the all-hands under 45 minutes total; people get fatigued.
- Exec asks must map to measurable KRs in the next sprint cycle. No vague promises.
- Push hard to reduce cross-team dependencies that add cascade risk.

QUICK LINKS
---
- Reset week tracker: ENG-3142
- Pre-read folder: drive/shared/reset-week/pre-reads (placeholder)
- Decision triage rubric: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Decision+Triage+Rubric

FEEDBACK LOG (please annotate inline below)
---
- Use comments for concrete changes. If you disagree with a tradeoff, propose alternate micro-OKRs with quantification.

END - working draft (v0.1)
---
Next: consolidate pre-reads into a single 4-page summary, lock run-of-show, publish cadence for follow-ups.
